groups.name: Wingman / Battle Buddy Support & Teamwork
items: Willingly helps classmates study, shares notes, and ensures no one gets left behind on coursework.
Voluntarily pitches in during barracks/dorm GI parties, cleaning details, and accountability formations without complaining.
Builds a positive environment in the squad/flight and avoids cliques, gossip, or unnecessary drama.
Looks out for classmates’ well-being and steps in to prevent peers from making bad decisions off-duty.

groups.name: Standards, Discipline & Military Bearing
items: Always at the right place, at the right time, in the right uniform, with the right gear.
Consistently maintains sharp uniform standards, haircuts/grooming, and barracks/dorm room cleanliness.
Follows phase privileges, curfew, and training rules even when Drill Sergeants or MTLs are not around.
Puts forth maximum effort during morning PT and encourages struggling teammates during workouts.

groups.name: Classroom & Training Professionalism
items: Stays awake, attentive, and respectful toward instructors during long blocks of technical instruction.
Handles academic pressure, inspections, and corrective training with maturity and a positive attitude.
Accepts feedback from instructors and student leaders respectfully without making excuses.

groups.name: Student Leadership Potential
items: Sets a standard of behavior that naturally motivates other trainees to do the right thing.
Relays information from cadre/student leaders accurately and clearly to the rest of the group.
Remains calm and organized when placed in charge of marching formations, study groups, or daily tasks.

rubric: Frequently violates rules, brings down morale, or requires constant supervision from peers and cadre.
Occasionally slips on standards, struggles with time management, or avoids shared duties.
Reliable battle buddy/wingman; follows rules, passes evaluations, and pulls their own weight.
Proactive teammate; helps others study, maintains high bearing, and steps up during details.
Role model trainee; elevates the entire platoon/flight and embodies military core values daily.

leadership.title: Student Leadership
leadership.prompt: Would you trust this Soldier/Airman to be your Squad Leader, Flight Leader, or Rope? Why or why not?

blindspot.title: Blind Spots
blindspot.prompt: What is one habit this trainee needs to fix before arriving at their first operational duty station?
